abstract: In nature, plants experience frequently changing light conditions. To balance photoprotection and photosynthetic efficiency, chloroplasts dynamically regulate proton-motive force (PMF) partitioning through thylakoid ion transport proteins. While the roles of K+ and Cl- transport in PMF regulation are established in Arabidopsis thaliana, the contribution of Na+ flux remains unexplored. Here, we identify NHD1 as a thylakoid-localized transporter that mediates pH-dependent Na+/H+ antiport in a heterologous system with a Km of approximately 2 mM. Unlike other characterized thylakoid ion transport proteins, NHD1 loss does not alter photosynthesis when plants are grown under control light. However, prolonged fluctuating-light exposure uncovered pronounced physiological consequences of NHD1 deficiency: null mutants exhibit delayed non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation, reduced photosystem II quantum yield, altered chloroplast ultrastructure, and significantly impaired growth. Also, higher-order mutants lacking NHD1, K+/H+ exchanger KEA3, and voltage-dependent chloride channel VCCN1, exhibit stronger photosynthetic responses than the respective single mutants, suggesting partial functional redundancy among these thylakoid ion transporters. Together, our findings establish Na+/H+ exchange via NHD1 as a previously unrecognized, conserved component of thylakoid ion homeostasis, highlighting its importance for long-term photosynthetic acclimation to dynamic light environments, and expanding the repertoire of PMF-regulating transporters.

metadata.title: Na+/H+ antiport across the thylakoid membrane is functionally conserved in the Chloroplastida Arabidopsis

summary: NHD1, a thylakoid Na+/H+ antiporter in Arabidopsis, supports photosynthetic acclimation to fluctuating light and shows partial redundancy with KEA3 and VCCN1.
title: Na+/H+ antiport across the thylakoid membrane is functionally conserved in the Chloroplastida Arabidopsis
